subject: SD-20-015
comment: If I measured the proposed plot correctly Lot #1 is to be roughly 50 feet wide and 200 feet long. I would oppose the planning commission acceptance of such a peculiar shaped property for a building lot. Can you imagine what a subdivision of 50 foot wide deep lots would look like?

subject: ZM-20-007 and SD-20-015
comment: I am very opposed to both proposals of rezoning and adding at least two new building sites. New zoning would allow less property for building sites and increase the possibilities of more homes. I am opposed to any new subdivision for different reasons. I have lived directly south at 3512 Hillside Lane for 50 years. Our two properties are heavily wooded and part of East Millcreek. A subdivision would destroy some of the wooded area. The other reason I oppose is there is a sharp bend in the road right at 3500 S Hillside Lane. It would increase the current danger by adding another driveway way and increasing the homes and number of cars at that part of the bend. My wife and I walk past the area on our walk and are well aware of an accident waiting to happen. Cars travel much to fast around the bend. Please, please use wisdom in considering what is best for our community. Sincerely, Dean and Donna Jarman

Millcreek Planning Commission, I would like to express my concerns for the proposed project off of Hillside Lane. My family and myself are against this project. Our concerns are mainly the danger of additional traffic and driveways. The congestion is already a frequent issue of safety when walking and riding bicycles in the area and we can only see it compounded should this plan be completed. The loss of trees is also of concern. Hate to lose the aesthetic of the neighborhood. (So many trees have already been lost due to the beetles.) Thank you for considering our objections. We appreciate your fairness and time when working on our neighborhood planning.

subject: Subdivision on 3500 S. Hillside Lane
comment: There is an application for a rezone as a preface to a subdivision at subject address. Do you then approve a subdivision application before the community sees the renderings of what's being proposed ? It seems that the proposed 3 lots are 'interesting', 2 of the new lots are slivers that would contain a 'small' house; not sure what small means. The 2 lot would be larger and contain the existing home. I think we should see a proposal of the layout of the homes as to size, shape, style, etc. before approving a subdivision 1. Traffic is a concern because of the 3/4 schools in the area; Hillside is a narrow, country lane that has the sharp turn right where the entry to the lot(s) are/would be. 2. Concern over the density of the homes in that area, 3 lots may be okay, but the document I saw, indicates 2 small slivers and 1 larger lot. Would want to see more specifics on what the applicant is proposing. 3. I might be concerned over the look and size/scale and height of the homes; having no document that gives us the layout, I can't give specifics at this time. 4. Concern over the creek and development; we have seen several along the creek that have caused concern with residents, encroachment, deterioration of stream bank with removal of trees and construction; e.g., the large home on the 's' curve, the development on Honeycutt (at Millcreek Way), property across creek from the community center. 5. The trees, a major asset to the stream - will they be removed and how many ? Will trees be required to be planted to replace those removed during construction. We had a development where trees were removed because they were 'infested' w/o providing proof they were infested. 6. What will be the impact to neighbors across the creek; in terms of what will they be seeing? How will it change the quiet, calm sense of the creek and those residents who live along the stream ..
